title: Durable performance operations and admission
boundary_reason: Owns application operation kinds, admission, durable execution, cancellation, failure mapping, and server composition.
behavioral_concerns: Cancellation, classified failures, semantic outcomes, and run identities must remain distinct and inspectable.

Start, resume, recover, and cancel must preserve durable ownership and writer fencing.

theories.claim: Production TUI and web composition paths can silently discard invalid performance configuration through sharedOperationRunner.
theories.basis: Although sharedOperationRunner discards the local performanceSettings error, both supplied production composition paths validate performanceSettings before constructing the runner: runTUI returns ExitConfig on failure, and runServe returns ExitConfig on failure [qa-v1-block-539767426a292f490828efde, qa-v1-block-2e7cabc506be3c6ebc4c4910, qa-v1-block-ebd21cdd229fbe3af0d1930e, qa-v1-block-da24117cc66e2742d5a2bd79].
theories.confirmation_condition: A production TUI or web path constructs sharedOperationRunner without first successfully validating performanceSettings.
theories.refutation_condition: Each production TUI and web construction path returns a configuration error before constructing sharedOperationRunner when performanceSettings fails.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Another production sharedOperationRunner construction path exists outside the supplied composition paths.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Compare the frozen TUI and serve composition flow with the runner initialization; no execution is required.

theories.claim: The new public performance CLI surface lacks compatibility tests for stable JSON envelopes, text output, stdout/stderr behavior, and semantic exit-code mappings.
theories.basis: The performance CLI adds JSON and text presentation plus distinct exit mappings, while the supplied performance tests cover argument admission, DTO filtering, and fixture-name presence; the expanded command test excerpt covers comparable help and repair contracts but does not show performance output or exit compatibility coverage, and the current conformance review records the same gap [qa-v1-block-a1c54f69a34aba9ad20c1302, qa-v1-block-16640fcab12eba4718294df9, qa-v1-block-5a540b46eca643bf6640a391, qa-v1-block-ab144792f62973cd0e5baaf1, qa-v1-block-afc7f1a02ec78c68dd9233f4].
theories.confirmation_condition: Performance command tests do not assert stable JSON/text output, stdout/stderr separation, and exit mappings for target miss, cancellation, partial completion, and operational failure.
theories.refutation_condition: Compatibility tests exercise those public performance output and exit-code contracts.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Uncited test content demonstrates complete equivalent compatibility coverage despite the current conformance review finding.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Use static test-source inspection only; no runtime or repository mutation is needed.
